description: A new Public Citizen report reveals that corporations bankrolling Trump's $400 million White House ballroom have been rewarded with over $50 billion in federal contracts in six months. Fourteen of 27 known donors saw their government business surge — while the DOJ dropped enforcement actions against them.

faqs.answer: According to Public Citizen's Ballroom Billions report released June 4, 2026, fourteen of twenty-seven known corporate donors received over $50 billion in new or expanded federal contracts in just six months.
faqs.question: How much have Trump's ballroom donors received in federal contracts?

faqs.answer: Lockheed Martin received approximately $43.8 billion, Booz Allen Hamilton received over $4.2 billion, and Palantir received just over $1 billion. Other beneficiaries include Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Caterpillar, T-Mobile, Meta, Apple, and Nvidia.
faqs.question: Which companies received the most in contracts?

faqs.answer: Trump's $400 million vanity construction project to build a ballroom on the White House grounds after demolishing the East Wing. Americans oppose it 2-to-1. Corporate donors are funding it through a secret agreement that allows anonymous contributions.
faqs.question: What is the White House ballroom project?

faqs.answer: Sixteen of twenty-seven known corporate donors are facing federal enforcement actions, including antitrust reviews, securities charges, and labor disputes. Under the Trump DOJ, several of these cases have been dropped or reduced.
faqs.question: Have any enforcement actions against these donors been dropped?

leadParagraph: A watchdog report from Public Citizen has revealed that more than half of the corporate donors to Donald Trump's $400 million White House ballroom project have received over $50 billion in new or expanded federal contracts in just six months, while the Trump DOJ simultaneously dropped or reduced enforcement actions against many of those same companies.

mainImage.alt: Construction equipment and scaffolding surround the partially demolished East Wing of the White House with exposed structural beams and debris
mainImage.caption: Demolition continues on the East Wing of the White House in Washington, D.C., on October 21, 2025, to make way for President Trump's proposed $400 million ballroom project.

methodology: Reported using the Public Citizen 'Ballroom Billions' report (June 4, 2026), Washington Post coverage, The New Republic analysis, Common Dreams reporting, and Spokesman-Review coverage. All data sourced directly from Public Citizen's analysis of federal contracting records and corporate donation disclosures.
title: Trump Ballroom Donors Receive $50 Billion in Federal Contracts — Pay-to-Play Exposed
